primaryAuthorityEvidence.observed: The current judiciary page describes Veterans Treatment Court and states it is subject to evaluation under §16-10-139; the program remains operational.

16-90-1601: Specialty court program includes a veterans treatment specialty court program under §16-101-101 et seq.
16-90-1602_a: After successful completion, a specialty-court judge may order dismissal and sealing if the prosecutor recommended dismissal and sealing and the judge considered past criminal history and found dismissal/sealing appropriate.
16-90-1602_b: Sealing follows the Comprehensive Criminal Record Sealing Act; a specialty-court judge may enter the sealing order immediately upon completion; there is no limit to previous felony convictions under §16-90-1406(c)(1).
16-90-1602_d: For a conviction entered by another court of the same level, the participant must complete the specialty program and the other sentence, and the other court must agree and sign the uniform sealing order.

formComparison.obligation: Current statutory citation and route identity
formEvidence: Both titles cite §16-101-106 and §16-90-1401 (petition text lines 16-19; order text lines 16-19).
The petition’s primary prayer cites §16-98-303 and its separate-offense prayer cites §16-101-106(b)(1) (petition lines 74-80).
The order’s grant cites §16-101-106 and its separate-offense order cites §16-101-106(b)(1) (order lines 70-79).
formComparison.currentRule: Act 691 repeals §16-101-106 and places the specialty-court dismissal/sealing rule at §16-90-1602.
formComparison.finding: The held binaries are exact official source bytes, but their participant-facing/legal citations are stale against enacted law. The §16-98-303 primary prayer is also a drug-court citation and needs an owner/counsel decision before any generated packet or guide uses it.

formEvidence: Petition and order require successful program completion and record its date (petition lines 38-45; order lines 36-40).
Both require a prosecuting-attorney recommendation for dismissal and sealing.
formComparison.currentRule: §16-90-1602(a) uses the same completion and prosecutor-recommendation concepts and additionally requires the judge to consider past criminal history and determine dismissal/sealing appropriate.
formComparison.finding: The completion/recommendation inputs align. The order has a rehabilitation checkbox but no explicit current-law finding that the judge considered criminal history and found dismissal/sealing appropriate; whether the official form is sufficient or must be accompanied by a current-law statement is unresolved.

formEvidence: Both forms state that proceedings were deferred without a judgment of guilt and the defendant was placed on probation/court supervision (petition lines 29-31; order lines 28-30).
formComparison.currentRule: Act 58 §16-101-102(e) expressly allows a veterans treatment specialty court program to be pre-adjudication or post-adjudication; §16-90-1602 is written for a participant’s successful completion without a pre-adjudication limitation.
formComparison.finding: The held pair describes a pre-adjudication fact pattern and does not establish coverage for post-adjudication veterans-court participants. Owner/counsel must decide whether this pair is intentionally pre-adjudication-only, whether a separate current post-adjudication ACIC pair exists, or how an ACIC-controlled product may lawfully cover both.

formEvidence: The optional branch asks for a prior guilty/nolo/found-guilty offense in another circuit court, requires target-group status, lists four exclusions, and requests another judge’s concurrence (petition lines 52-64 and 77-80; order lines 47-59 and 75-79).
formComparison.currentRule: §16-90-1602(d) requires completion of the specialty program, completion of the other court’s sentence, and the other court’s agreement plus signature on the uniform sealing order; it distinguishes circuit-court and district-court convictions.
formComparison.finding: The old target-group/exclusion/concurrence branch cannot be assumed to be the current §16-90-1602(d) contract. The sentence-completion input, same-level court rule, uniform-order signature, and treatment of the old exclusions require an explicit owner/counsel mapping.

formEvidence: Neither held form states the new immediate-order permission or the removal of the prior-felony-count limit.
formComparison.currentRule: §16-90-1602(b) permits immediate sealing upon completion and removes the §16-90-1406(c)(1) prior-felony limit for this route.
formComparison.finding: The current participant guidance must carry these rules if the route is adopted; they are not a reason to alter the source binaries without an approved form strategy.

formEvidence: The pair asks for completion, case facts, and status facts but does not ask for adult status, veteran/service-member status, qualifying disorder, or policy-compliance evidence.
formComparison.currentRule: Act 58 §16-101-103 states the program eligibility elements; the route design separates program participation guidance from the post-completion petition/order.
formComparison.finding: The owner must decide whether stage-1 guidance/participant attestations supply these program facts, or whether stage-2 packet generation must require completion/admission records beyond the two current generation questions.

formComparison.obligation: Service, notice, filing fee, and waiver
formEvidence: The petition certificate of service names the prosecuting or city attorney and arresting agency (petition lines 128-143).
The order directs transmission to ACIC, AOC, prosecutor/city attorney, district clerk if applicable, and arresting agency, citing §16-90-1413 (order lines 81-86).
formComparison.currentRule: §16-90-1602(b) incorporates the Comprehensive Criminal Record Sealing Act procedures but does not itself state the memo’s three-day service or 30-day objection timing. Act 58 §16-101-104 addresses program costs/fees and indigency waivers, not a definitive filing fee for this petition.
formComparison.finding: The three-day/30-day participant instructions, exact service recipients, filing fee, and fee-waiver route need a current procedural/owner determination; no fee or waiver fact is invented here.

resolvedFactualInputs: The original current-statute blocker is resolved factually: §16-101-106 was repealed by Act 691, and §16-90-1602 is the enacted specialty-court dismissal/sealing rule that includes veterans treatment court through §16-90-1601(6).
The historical missing-pair blocker is resolved in custody: the exact petition and order binaries are both present and SHA-256 verified; the order is bound by SOURCE_RECOVERY_WAVE1 to the family.
The veterans treatment court program remains an active Arkansas Judiciary program; the route itself was not repealed.
The ACIC public page still publishes the July 27, 2021 pair under its old §16-101-106 title. That is a current publication fact, not proof that the old statutory citation remains operative.
